The complex magnetic permeability and dielectric permittivity spectra of the MnZn ferrite-rubber composites were measured in the frequency range of 2 to 18 GHz.
The MnZn ferrite volume fractions studied range from 0 to 0.37.
The complex permeability and permittivity generally increase with increasing ferrite volume fraction, with some exceptions at higher frequencies above 14 GHz for the permittivity.
The reflection loss decreases (i.e. absorption increases) with increasing ferrite volume fraction, reaching a minimum of -35 dB for a ferrite volume fraction of 0.20.
Increasing the RAM thickness generally shifts the frequency of minimum reflection loss to lower values.
The RAM with 0.20 ferrite volume fraction has a frequency bandwidth of 4.5 GHz for RL < -10 dB.
The lattice constant of the prepared MnZn ferrite is 8.483 Å.
The density of the MnZn ferrite is 5.029 g/cm^3, and the density of the silicone rubber is 1.28 g/cm^3.
The stoichiometry of the prepared MnZn ferrite is Mn0.66Zn0.34Fe2O4.
The MnZn ferrite particles were prepared by the usual ceramic sintering method from the mixture of Fe2O3, MnCO3 and ZnO.
Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) examinations showed that the MnZn ferrite particles have a variety of sizes (1 - 50 μm) and shapes (acicular or plate).
The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern confirmed the existence of a single cubic phase for the MnZn ferrite, in agreement with the JCPDS card (74-2401).
The pure silicone rubber (0 vol% ferrite) has real permeability and permittivity values of around 1 and 3, respectively, with low magnetic and dielectric losses.
The frequency of the minimum reflection loss is shifted to lower frequencies as the MnZn ferrite volume fraction increases.
The RAM samples with different ferrite contents exhibit a single-peaked-minimum curve for the reflection loss.
